reason: Attack failed against the 1706 sheets themselves. I downloaded the Internet Archive scan reflectionsuponm00aste and read the Preface rather than taking the verifier's report. The passage is at lines 461 to 470, under the running head The Preface, and reads, through the long s of the scan, If all Men are born free, how is it that all Women are born Slaves? as they must be if the being subjected to the inconstant, uncertain, unknown, arbitrary Will of Men, be the perfect Condition of Slavery? So the capital S on Slaves is confirmed, and so is the widespread shorter variant being wrong: Astell wrote how is it that all Women are born Slaves, not why are all Women born Slaves. The truncation at the question mark leaves a complete interrogative sentence and does not misrepresent the argument, since what follows is Astell's gloss on the same question. Title: the scan's title page reads REFLECTIONS UPON MARRIAGE, The Third Edition, To which is Added A Preface, in Answer to some Objections, so dropping Some from the 1700 title is correct for this edition and is not a slip. Imprint: the title page's damaged line resolves to Printed for R. Wilkin at the King's Head in St. Paul's Church-Yard, 1706, which matches the edition field, and Wilkin was Astell's publisher. Locator: the Preface added to the third edition is the right locator and is better than the page of a modern reprint the proposal originally carried, because the sentence exists in 1706 and the Springborg pagination is a later artefact. Attribution: Astell's own prose in her own book, no speaker owed, and she is not on the misattribution list. shipped.js: no exact match, no near match, Astell stands at zero of three, not banned. Scope: 1706, not scripture, not oratory despite its polemical voice, not a proverb, not business writing. Publishable: Slaves is metaphor about marriage, there is no graphic content and no warning is owed. Source line 82 characters, leads with the name, no dash. Tag Essay is the form of the work. One observation for the editor that is not a refutation, since theme fit is not the refuter's ground: of the four this is the loosest fit to Courage in Trial, being a challenge that names an injustice rather than a line about holding through one, and it will read as a justice line on the card.
